title: Strictly Palindromic Number
summary: Determine if an integer n is strictly palindromic by checking if its representation in every base b from 2 to n-2 is a palindrome.
statement: Determine if an integer n is strictly palindromic by checking if its representation in every base b from 2 to n-2 is a palindrome. Return true if all bases yield a palindromic string, otherwise return false.
constraints: A strictly palindromic number would be palindromic in every base from two through n-2.
Return whether n satisfies that condition.
hints: It is enough to find one required base that always fails.
Consider base n-2 for every n at least four.
n equals 1*(n-2)+2, so its representation is 12, except n=4 where base two is 100; neither is palindromic.
Thus every permitted n has a concrete failing base and the result is always false.
editorial: Thus every permitted n has a concrete failing base and the result is always false.

tests.explanation: In base seven, nine is represented as 12, which is not a palindrome.
In base two, four is 100, so it is not strictly palindromic.
